tasks.title: Codex multi-agent runs collapse into one session
tasks.historyNote: The session that found it while mining real Codex histories had already traced which session_meta field each subagent's rollout carries.
tasks.prompt:
Codex Desktop multi-agent runs are broken in the index: a real run of 15 agents shows up as a single session, and 14 of the agents' work cannot be found. Each subagent writes its own rollout file.

Fix the Codex adapter (src/adapters/codex.ts) so that every subagent is listed as its own session by listSessions(), and listTurns(<subagent id>) returns that subagent's own turns, not its parent's. Older rollouts that carry only one id must keep working. Add a test.

tasks.title: Outcome records count injected text as requests
tasks.historyNote: Fully specified: the history holds where the noise was seen, nothing the task needs.
tasks.prompt:
Session outcome records still count some injected text as if the user had asked it. userUtterance (src/outcomes/outcome.ts) must return null for:
- Codex turn-aborted notices (text starting with <turn_aborted>),
- skill bodies (starting with <skill>),
- Codex's automatic approval reviewer prompt (starting with "The following is the Codex agent history"),
- in-app browser turns that carry only page context (starting with <in-app-browser-context).
An in-app browser turn that contains "## My request:" should yield the text after it, the way Codex IDE turns with "## My request for Codex:" already do. Add tests.

tasks.title: Hold the result token budget; add a session task digest
tasks.historyNote: Earlier sessions discussed serving outcome records instead of raw windows, and how results are packaged.
tasks.prompt:
Two problems with what a search hands an agent.

1. The token budget does not hold: a hit turn longer than maxTokens (a pasted log, a long reply) is sent whole; on real history some hits run 9x over. Make each result's window fit maxTokens (about 4 characters per token): keep the hit turn, add neighbouring turns nearest-first only while they fit, and if the hit turn alone is over the budget, cut it to the stretch holding the most query terms. Export focusOn(text: string, terms: string[], maxChars: number): string from src/search/search.ts: text unchanged when it fits; otherwise at most maxChars characters, the stretch with the most occurrences of the (lowercase) terms, with a leading and/or trailing "…" where it was cut; with no term present, the start of the text followed by "…".

2. An agent handed a hit has no overview of the session it came from. Add taskDigest(o: SessionOutcome, opts?: { matchedSeqs?: number[]; maxChars?: number }): string to src/outcomes/outcome.ts: one line per task that has a request, "N. <request> [<status>; <file names>]" (N counts from 1; file names without their folders), with " <- hit" on each task that contains a matched seq. Default budget 1200 characters, never exceeded; when too long, shorten each request before dropping anything, so the early requests stay listed. searchOnce puts it on each session's first result as outcome.digest, with all of that session's hits marked; that session's other results carry no digest.
Add tests.

tasks.title: Task digest built around the matched tasks
tasks.historyNote: The graded failure analysis that motivated it (long sessions cut before the matching task; hits that are the user's request without the agent's answer) is in the session just before.
tasks.prompt:
The task digest (taskDigest in src/outcomes/outcome.ts) loses what matters in long sessions: it lists tasks from the top until its character budget runs out, so the task that matched a search can be cut, and it never says what the agent actually did about a request. Rework it around the matched tasks.

- Each task in buildOutcome(...).tasks gets reply: the agent's last message in that task, as a Cite like the other citations, or null.
- taskDigest(o, { matchedSeqs, maxChars }) (maxChars default 1500) always shows every matched task in full, as "N. <request> [<status>; <files>] <- hit" followed by a line "   agent: <reply excerpt>" (three spaces, then "agent: "). Tasks that are not hits keep the one-line form, without a reply.
- The rest of the budget goes to the tasks nearest a hit; tasks left out are counted in a line like "… 12 more task(s)". The digest never exceeds maxChars.
- Existing lines keep their format, e.g. "1. fix the flaky websocket test [verified; a.ts]".
Update the tests.
